provider_query: MDN page for the Request.redirect property
answer:
The MDN page for **Request.redirect** is:

**https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Request/redirect**

`Request.redirect` is a read-only property of the Fetch API `Request` interface. It holds how redirects are handled: `"follow"`, `"error"`, or `"manual"`. The default is `"follow"`. It is widely available (since March 2017) and usable in Web Workers. [web:8]

### Relevant results

1. **Request: redirect property (MDN, English)** — Canonical page: values `follow` / `error` / `manual`, default `follow`, example with `new Request("flowers.jpg")`.  
   https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Request/redirect [web:8]

2. **Request interface (MDN)** — Parent page; lists `Request.redirect` among instance properties as the redirect-handling mode (`follow`, `error`, or `manual`).  
   https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Request [web:9]

3. **MDN source (GitHub)** — Source for the English page (`files/en-us/web/api/request/redirect/index.md`), including the same values, default, and example.  
   https://github.com/mdn/content/blob/main/files/en-us/web/api/request/redirect/index.md [web:1]

4. **Response.redirected (MDN)** — Related property on `Response` that reports whether a response came from a redirect. MDN recommends setting `redirect: "error"` on `fetch()` rather than only checking `redirected` after the fact.  
   https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected [web:2]

5. **Redirections in HTTP (MDN)** — Background on HTTP 3xx redirects and the `Location` header (not the `Request.redirect` API itself).  
   https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Redirections [web:10]

6. **Japanese MDN translation** — Same property page in Japanese.  
   https://developer.mozilla.org/ja/docs/Web/API/Request/redirect [web:4]

7. **Chinese MDN mirror** — Same content in Chinese.  
   https://mdn.org.cn/en-US/docs/Web/API/Request/redirect [web:3]

8. **Bun reference** — Documents `Request.redirect` as `readonly redirect: RequestRedirect`, with a link back to MDN.  
   https://bun.com/reference/globals/Request/redirect [web:6]

fetched.content:
- [Skip to main content](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected#content) - [Skip to search](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected#mdn-search) Learn frontend, backend, and AI from our course partner [Scrimba](https://scrimba.com/learn/frontend?via=mdn) # Response: redirected property Baseline Widely available This feature is well established and works across many devices and browser versions. It’s been available across browsers since October 2017. - [See full compatibility](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected#browser_compatibility) - [Learn more](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Baseline/Compatibility) **Note:** This feature is available in [Web Workers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Workers_API). The **`redirected`** read-only property of the [`Response`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response) interface indicates whether or not the response is the result of a request you made which was redirected. **Note:** Checking `redirected` to prevent redirects is not recommended, because by the time a response is received, the redirect has already happened, and you may have sent the request to an unintended destination, potentially sending sensitive information. Instead, you should do the filtering when you call [`fetch()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/fetch "fetch()"). See the example [Disallowing redirects](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected#disallowing_redirects), which shows this being done. ## [Value](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected\#value) A boolean value which is `true` if the response indicates that your request was redirected. ## [Examples](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected\#examples) ### [Detecting redirects](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected\#detecting_redirects) Checking to see if the response comes from a redirected request is as simple as checking this flag on the [`Response`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response) object. In the code below, a textual message is inserted into an element when a redirect occurred during the fetch operation. Note, however, that this isn't as safe as outright rejecting redirects if they're unexpected, as described under [Disallowing redirects](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected#disallowing_redirects) below. The [`url`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/url "url") property returns the final URL after redirects. jsCopy ``` fetch("awesome-picture.jpg") .then((response) => { const elem = document.getElementById("warning-message-box"); elem.textContent = response.redirected ? "Unexpected redirect" : ""; // final url obtained after redirects console.log(response.url); return response.blob(); }) .then((imageBlob) => { const imgObjectURL = URL.createObjectURL(imageBlob); document.getElementById("img-element-id").src = imgObjectURL; }); ``` ### [Disallowing redirects](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected\#disallowing_redirects) Checking `redirected` is a bad way to prevent redirects, because the redirect has already happened. Instead, you should set the redirect mode to `"error"` in the `options` parameter when calling [`fetch()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/fetch "fetch()"), like this: jsCopy ``` fetch("awesome-picture.jpg", { redirect: "error" }) .then((response) => response.blob()) .then((imageBlob) => { const imgObjectURL = URL.createObjectURL(imageBlob); document.getElementById("img-element-id").src = imgObjectURL; }); ``` ## [Specifications](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Response/redirected\#specifications) | Specification | | --- | | [Fetch\
